<SCRATCHPAD_REASONING>
Brad has provided a list of times when Elena and David are available. I need to check these times against Priya's and Marcus's calendars to find a common slot.

Here's the list from Brad:
*   Mon: 11:00, 11:30
*   Tue: 09:00, 09:30
*   Wed: 13:00, 13:30
*   Thu: 09:30, 14:30, 15:00
*   Fri: 15:00, 15:30

Now, I'll check my notes on Priya's and Marcus's calendars.

**Priya's busy times:**
*   Mon: 11:00-11:30 (Travel)
*   Tue: 09:00-09:30 (Board prep), 09:30-10:00 (Partner lunch)
*   Wed: 13:00-13:30 (Client call - Harbor Logistics), 13:30-14:00 (Client dinner prep)
*   Thu: 09:30-10:00 (Busy), 14:30-15:00 (Free), 15:00-15:30 (Client dinner prep)
*   Fri: 15:00-15:30 (Hiring panel), 15:30-16:00 (Contract review - Weller Group)

**Marcus's busy times:**
*   Mon: No conflict at 11:00, but busy 11:30-12:00
*   Tue: 09:00-09:30 (Recruiting call), 09:30-10:00 (Litigation strategy)
*   Wed: 13:00-13:30 (Partner lunch), 13:30-14:00 (Litigation strategy)
*   Thu: 09:30-10:00 (Contract review - Weller Group), 14:30-15:00 (Dentist appointment), 15:00-15:30 (Board prep)
*   Fri: 15:00-15:30 (Travel), 15:30-16:00 (Busy)

Let's go through the list from Brad one by one:
*   Mon 11:00: Priya is busy (Travel).
*   Mon 11:30: Priya is busy (Contract review), Marcus is busy.
*   Tue 09:00: Priya is busy (Board prep), Marcus is busy (Recruiting call).
*   Tue 09:30: Priya is busy (Partner lunch), Marcus is busy (Litigation strategy).
*   Wed 13:00: Priya is busy (Client call), Marcus is busy (Partner lunch).
*   Wed 13:30: Priya is busy (Client dinner prep), Marcus is busy (Litigation strategy).
*   Thu 09:30: Priya is busy (Busy), Marcus is busy (Contract review).
*   Thu 14:30: Priya is free. Marcus is busy (Dentist appointment).
*   Thu 15:00: Priya is busy (Client dinner prep), Marcus is busy (Board prep).
*   Fri 15:00: Priya is busy (Hiring panel), Marcus is busy (Travel).
*   Fri 15:30: Priya is busy (Contract review), Marcus is busy.

It seems none of the slots proposed by Brad work. I need to let Brad know this and suggest a new approach. Since we've both checked our respective pairs' calendars, the next logical step is to combine all the busy times to find a common free slot.

I will send a message to Brad explaining the situation and providing the full availability of Priya and Marcus. This will allow him to cross-reference with Elena's and David's availability to find a solution.

First I'll list all 30 minute slots from Mon-Fri 9-5, then remove the busy ones for Priya and Marcus.

Total slots: 5 days * 8 hours/day * 2 slots/hour = 80 slots

Priya's busy slots:
Mon: 10:00, 10:30, 11:00, 11:30, 12:00, 12:30, 14:00, 14:30, 15:00, 15:30, 16:00, 16:30 (12)
Tue: 9:00, 9:30, 10:00, 11:00, 11:30, 12:00, 12:30, 14:00, 15:00, 15:30, 16:00 (11)
Wed: 9:00, 9:30, 10:00, 10:30, 11:00, 11:30, 12:00, 13:00, 13:30, 14:00, 14:30, 16:00, 16:30 (13)
Thu: 9:30, 10:30, 11:00, 11:30, 12:00, 12:30, 13:30, 14:00, 15:00, 15:30, 16:00, 16:30 (12)
Fri: 9:00, 9:30, 10:00, 10:30, 12:00, 12:30, 13:30, 14:30, 15:00, 15:30, 16:00, 16:30 (12)
Total Priya busy: 60 slots

Marcus's busy slots:
Mon: 10:00, 10:30, 11:30, 12:00, 12:30, 13:00, 13:30, 14:00, 14:30, 15:30, 16:00, 16:30 (12)
Tue: 9:00, 9:30, 10:00, 10:30, 11:30, 12:00, 12:30, 14:00, 14:30, 15:00, 16:00 (11)
Wed: 9:30, 10:00, 10:30, 11:00, 11:30, 12:30, 13:00, 13:30, 14:30, 16:00, 16:30 (11)
Thu: 9:00, 9:30, 10:30, 11:00, 11:30, 12:30, 13:00, 14:00, 14:30, 15:00, 15:30, 16:00, 16:30 (13)
Fri: 9:00, 9:30, 10:00, 10:30, 12:00, 12:30, 13:00, 13:30, 14:00, 15:00, 15:30, 16:00, 16:30 (13)
Total Marcus busy: 60 slots

Let's find the union of their busy slots.
Mon: 10:00, 10:30, 11:00, 11:30, 12:00, 12:30, 13:00, 13:30, 14:00, 14:30, 15:00, 15:30, 16:00, 16:30
Tue: 9:00, 9:30, 10:00, 10:30, 11:00, 11:30, 12:00, 12:30, 14:00, 14:30, 15:00, 15:30, 16:00
Wed: 9:00, 9:30, 10:00, 10:30, 11:00, 11:30, 12:00, 12:30, 13:00, 13:30, 14:00, 14:30, 16:00, 16:30
Thu: 9:00, 9:30, 10:30, 11:00, 11:30, 12:00, 12:30, 13:00, 13:30, 14:00, 14:30, 15:00, 15:30, 16:00, 16:30
Fri: 9:00, 9:30, 10:00, 10:30, 12:00, 12:30, 13:00, 13:30, 13:30, 14:00, 14:30, 15:00, 15:30, 16:00, 16:30

This is getting complicated. I'll just list all the free times for Priya and Marcus.

Priya's free slots:
Mon: 9:00, 9:30, 13:00, 13:30
Tue: 10:30, 13:00, 13:30, 14:30, 16:30
Wed: 12:30, 15:00, 15:30
Thu: 9:00, 10:00, 13:00, 14:30
Fri: 11:00, 11:30, 13:00, 14:00

Marcus's free slots:
Mon: 9:00, 9:30, 11:00, 15:00
Tue: 11:00, 13:00, 13:30, 15:30, 16:30
Wed: 9:00, 12:00, 14:00, 15:00, 15:30
Thu: 10:00, 12:00
Fri: 11:00, 11:30, 14:30

Now I will check Brad's list against my free time lists.

Brad's list:
*   Mon: 11:00, 11:30 -> Priya is busy at 11:00 and 11:30.
*   Tue: 09:00, 09:30 -> Priya and Marcus are busy.
*   Wed: 13:00, 13:30 -> Priya is busy.
*   Thu: 09:30, 14:30, 15:00 -> Priya is busy at 9:30. Marcus is busy at 14:30 and 15:00. Priya is free at 14:30.
*   Fri: 15:00, 15:30 -> Priya and Marcus are busy.

My initial analysis was correct. None of the times work.
I will write a message to Brad.
I'll give him the list of free times for Priya and Marcus so he can compare with his pair.<SCRATCHPAD_REASONING>
Brad's proposed times didn't work. I need to collaborate with him to find a solution. I've already determined that none of the times he suggested are viable. The best way to move forward is to share the complete availability of Priya and Marcus with Brad. This will allow him to cross-reference with the calendars of Elena and David to find a time that works for everyone. I will send a message to the workspace with this information.

function.arguments:
{"text":"Thanks for checking, Brad. I've looked at the times you suggested, and unfortunately, none of them work for both Priya and Marcus.

Let's try a different approach. Here is a full list of all the 30-minute slots where Priya and Marcus are *both* free:

*   Mon: 09:00, 09:30
*   Tue: 13:00, 13:30, 16:30
*   Wed: 15:00, 15:30
*   Thu: 10:00
*   Fri: 11:00, 11:30

Could you please compare this with Elena's and David's availability and see if there are any overlaps? I'm hoping we can find a common time this way. If not, we may need to look for 60-minute free blocks and see if we can split them. But let's see if any of these work first."}
